page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.medium is an entry-tier virtual server provisioned on KVM hypervisor architecture. It features 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing an elevated memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. It does not bundle local disk storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote network-attached volumes for persistent data storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that compute throughput is modest. Synthetic processor metrics place both single-core and multi-core execution in the lower benchmark percentiles, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1743.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 2616.1. Memory bandwidth tests yield 17.2 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 14.52 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific throughput metrics demonstrate 2.52 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.49 GB/sec in static web serving capacity.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the instance provides high memory density on a low core footprint. The core architectural tradeoff is the constrained processing capacity of a single physical core, which limits performance during compute-heavy execution. Consequently, the ecs.e3.medium is best aligned with memory-sensitive yet CPU-light tasks, including intermediate caching tiers, staging environments, lightweight relational databases, and background memory queues.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.medium is a memory-oriented virtual instance configured with 2 vCPUs from a single hyper-threaded Intel Xeon 8269CY physical core operating at 2.5 GHz. It pairs 16.0 GB of memory with its dual-thread compute setup, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU profile. The server does not bundle local disk storage or included public IPv4 addresses, relying on external network storage. Benchmark evaluations record entry-level computational performance, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 1743.0 and a PassMark CPU rating of 2616.1, alongside uncached memory read bandwidth of 17.2 GB/sec. The instance delivers cost efficiency for workloads prioritizing memory footprint over raw calculation speed. It is suited for lightweight databases, in-memory caching layers, background job workers, and staging environments.
